text:
Cora: quick flag — noticed our weekly KPI deck shows a weird bump in webinar LTV projection after we applied the new sample-pruning rule on event ingestion. link: https://dash.redwood.ai/r/weekly/launch-metrics :eyes:

Vik: i saw that. sampling went from 15% -> 5% for older buckets, which reduces variance but also amplified a few high-value conversions in the extrapolation.

Samira: can you point to the pruning commit? i want to see the exact filter.

Vik: it's in analytics/ingest: commit 9f4c2a — we drop sessions with <2 events in the rolling window for sampled exports.

Pete: dropping low-activity sessions makes sense for quality, but the extrapolation code assumes random uniform sampling — pruning is not uniform and biases toward engaged users.

KPI-Bot: alert: sample_prune_bias detected (score 6.1) for webinar_ltv_projection on 2026-05-08 10:12 UTC.

Maya: ok action plan: 1) Vik revert pruning for the KPI snapshot rebuild; 2) Samira run A/B re-extrapolation (pruned vs full sample) and output a conservative metric for the deck; 3) Pete propose an adjusted extrapolation formula that weights by session_activity. target: updated snapshot before Friday deck.

Vik: reverting prune flag now for the analytics export pipeline. ETA 20m. leaving the change in a short-lived feature branch so we can compare.

Samira: running re-extrapolate job with both datasets. posting a short table in a min.

Pete: quick note on formulas — if pruning removes low-activity users we should downweight the extrapolation factor by p_engaged = sampled_engaged / sampled_total and apply a shrinkage term. i'll sketch it out.

```
adjusted_projection = raw_sum * (1 + shrink*(1 - p_engaged))
```

Cora: please keep the math simple in the deck. we need a conservative single-number view and an appendix with sensitivity.

Samira: posted numbers: full-sample extrapolation projects LTV = $18.9, pruned-sample projects LTV = $23.4. reweighted (Pete's shrinkage 0.3) gives $19.8. link to CSV: /shared/marketing/sampling-analysis/3276543210.csv

Vik: thanks. that's a big delta. looks like a few outlier purchases were retained in pruning.

Maya: for the weekly KPI slide let's use Pete's reweighted conservative number $19.8 and call out the sensitivity range ($18.9-$23.4) in the notes. add a short line: "metric sensitive to recent sampling change; see appendix for methodology".

Pete: i'll draft the appendix blurb and include the formula + recommended shrinkage defaults. also adding a small diagnostic to surface 'sampling_bias_index' on the dashboard.

Samira: uploaded the re-extrapolation outputs and a small explainer doc to /shared/marketing/sampling-analysis/3276543210-README.md.

Vik: reverted pipeline change and reprocessed yesterday's export. ETA for updated dashboard snapshot ~45m.

KPI-Bot: note added to weekly_kpi_review (2026-05-08): sampling-prune change created LTV projection bias; mitigation: revert, re-extrapolate, show conservative figure + sensitivity appendix. ref: https://dash.redwood.ai/r/notes/3276543210-sample-note

Cora: thanks team. follow-ups: 1) Pete to open a ticket for stable extrapolation logic; 2) Data & Growth to agree on a sampling policy doc so the dashboard doesn't silently change. we'll call this out in Friday's deck under 'Data caveats'.

Maya: agreed. please add the conservative number to slide 4 and append the appendix file. good catch. closing thread unless any other surprises. :lock:"
